fixture_name: Four-lane arterial improvement — US preliminary design (FHWA case study, PD)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Queuing/turning/parking interference at closely-spaced intersections is a classic preliminary-design safety issue on a corridor with recorded accident designations, giving real crash-risk substance.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal interference mechanism is supported by a verbatim quote (EV-US-016); minor gap that the 'high-accident designations' phrase in the scenario carries no separate citation.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed purely as a safety_concern with null normative basis, correctly avoiding any compliance/safety conflation and matching FHWA RSA concern semantics for the design stage.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Two concrete, stage-viable measures (turn restrictions, relocating stalls clear of the functional area) tied to the stated mechanisms, though it stops short of naming specific movements or stall groups.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists are explicitly acknowledged with an explicit scoping rationale to vehicle occupants, fitting the not-applicable-but-acknowledged case; parking-related sight-line effects on VRUs were not explored.

justifications.substance: Closely spaced signals (650 ft) on a corridor with recorded accident history creating queue-spillback/blocking risk is a classic, substantive preliminary-design-stage safety concern.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal spacing claim is supported by a verbatim quote from EV-US-001; the spillback mechanism is clearly labelled as a derived inference rather than invented content, though the 'high-accident designations' mention in the scenario lacks its own cited evidence_id.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a safety_concern under FHWA RSA preliminary-design semantics with no fabricated normative basis and no conflation of compliance questions with safety findings.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: signal coordination analysis plus Do Not Block Intersection signage and conspicuity enhancements are all viable deliverables at preliminary design; only mild vagueness in the conspicuity wording prevents no deduction here.
justifications.vru_coverage: Pedestrians and cyclists crossing both intersections are explicitly acknowledged with a stated scoping rationale, but potential VRU-specific impacts of spillback (e.g., crosswalk blockage trapping pedestrians) are not analyzed, matching the acknowledge-but-not-applicable band.
